title: Go-to-Market Signal Plan for Model Variant Additions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: coordinate a cross-team rollout for three new model variants (dense-8bit, quantized-4, and instruction-tuned-lite) into the public catalog. Scope covers catalog metadata, benchmark artifacts, release notes, SDK examples, console listing, marketing announcement draft, and observability dashboards + alerting for early regressions. Goals: a repeatable checklist that reduces last-minute blockers, ensures measurable quality signals (latency, regression rate, semantic quality delta), and provides clear rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog entries published with accurate metadata, tags, and model family mapping in the catalog UI and API
Benchmark dashboard created and populated (latency, throughput, cost-per-token, QA evaluation on 3 prompt suites)
Release notes draft reviewed and approved by legal, docs, and engineering; shipped with SDK examples
Marketing announcement copy + assets approved and scheduled; internal playbook for customer support prepared
Monitoring: dashboards, alerting thresholds, and a runbook for rollback/auto-fallback are in place and tested
Post-launch drift checks configured to detect quality regressions within 72 hours
tasks: PM: finalize catalog metadata spreadsheet and handoff to Catalog Engineering (link in attachments)
Eng: add model variants to serving manifest and verify kernel selection tags (PR: #1428)
Benchmarks: run full-speed suite across 4 region+hardware combos, capture median p90/p95 latency and cost; upload results to benchmark dashboard
Docs: write SDK examples for text generation + function calling patterns and a short migration guide for customers
Console: add model listing, per-model cost breakdown hooks, and configuration knobs for variant selection
Marketing: draft blog and one-pager; prepare social snippets and customer email cadence
Support: prepare triage playbook and canned responses for known trade-offs (e.g., slight tokenization differences)
Observability: add metrics (regression_rate, avg_latency_ms, error_rate, fallback_count), create alerts, and smoke test alerts
Legal & Security: confirm data handling language for model variants and KMS usage if required
Launch rehearsal: dry run with Canary cohort and simulate rollback flow
launch_signals: Quality: regression_rate <= 2% on curated eval set or immediate rollback
Latency: p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.2 (allow 20% headroom at launch)
Cost: observed cost-per-token within +/-15% of forecast for selected quantized variant
Reliability: error_rate < 0.5% and fallback_count below configured threshold
Adoption: 24h active API keys calling new variants >= 10 (smoke adoption signal)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal): publish catalog entries in staging and invite 3 internal partners to test
Phase 1 (Canary): route 2% of traffic to new variants with auto-fallback to stable family
Phase 2 (Gradual): 2% -> 10% -> 50% over 48h windows conditioned on launch signals
Phase 3 (General): promote to full availability if metrics remain green for 72h
rollback_criteria: If regression_rate > 2% over 1h window -> revert routing to previous model family
If p95 latency breaches 2x baseline persistently for 30 minutes -> revert
If error_rate > 1% for 15 minutes -> immediate rollback and postmortem
Customer escalations: any enterprise customer request for rollback triggers immediate pause and coordination with SE teams
